strengths: Addresses a genuine practical bottleneck in diffusion LM inference with substantial throughput improvements (4.4-5.3×) demonstrated on real hardware (H100)
Well-controlled empirical evaluation across three model scales (240M-1.3B) with identical training setup, data, and tokenization
First systematic study applying SSMs/Mamba to discrete diffusion language modeling, validating that iterative denoising does not inherently require attention
Comprehensive evaluation across multiple benchmarks (validation PPL on DCLM, zero-shot generalization on 7 datasets, downstream reasoning tasks)
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and thorough related work connecting vision diffusion, SSMs, and language modeling
Hybrid architecture shows consistent improvements over pure attention, suggesting complementary roles of attention and recurrence in diffusion
weaknesses: Limited novelty: primarily an architectural replacement (Transformers → Mamba) without algorithmic innovation; bidirectional fusion (Eq. 6) is trivial (forward+backward addition)

Critical missing ablations: no analysis of (a) why additive fusion is optimal for bidirectional Mamba, (b) sensitivity to K in hybrid model (fixed at K=5), (c) impact of d_state parameter, (d) alternative fusion strategies
Modeling quality gains are inconsistent and modest: DiffuTran remains competitive at 240M; at 1.3B, ~2% PPL improvement but comparable/worse performance on individual downstream tasks
Throughput measurements limited to batch size 1 on single GPU—fails to assess practical speedup in realistic multi-batch/distributed inference scenarios; unclear if benefits persist with batching

Only compared against Transformer baseline (DiffuTran); no comparison with recently proposed efficient alternatives (approximate KV-caching methods Wu et al. 2025, Ma et al. 2025, other efficient inference techniques)

Weak absolute downstream task performance at 1.3B scale (26-38% accuracy on challenging benchmarks) makes it difficult to assess whether quality-efficiency trade-off is acceptable; paper acknowledges scores are modest but doesn't investigate implications
No theoretical analysis of why SSMs should be effective denoisers beyond citing vision diffusion; limited intuition for the mechanisms enabling performance
Missing implementation details: exact Mamba-2 training kernel, reproducibility concerns (no code release mentioned), incomplete hyperparameter documentation

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three model scales with controlled setup (identical training data, tokenization, noise schedules), providing confident comparison of architectures
Excellent throughput analysis combining asymptotic complexity (Table 3) with extensive empirical measurements up to 65K tokens, demonstrating 8.2× improvements on long sequences
Insightful latency decomposition (Figure 3) that clearly isolates quadratic attention costs and explains Mamba's superior scaling behavior
Thorough breadth of evaluation: seven zero-shot datasets, five downstream reasoning tasks, and multiple inference algorithms (full-sequence and block-diffusion variants)
Well-motivated bidirectional Mamba architecture that preserves probabilistic semantics of masked diffusion while enabling linear-time inference
Clear presentation with good organization, informative visualizations, and honest discussion of limitations
weaknesses: Limited novelty: primarily combines two existing methods (Mamba + masked diffusion) without substantial architectural innovation; vision diffusion Mamba models already exist; bidirectional design is straightforward addition (Eq. 6)

Unjustified critical design choices lacking ablations: N=5 interleaving pattern (no sensitivity analysis), bidirectional fusion via simple addition (why not concatenation + projection?), halved MLP expansion ratio (impact uncharacterized)

Severe practical limitations: batch size B=1 throughout (not realistic for production), K=L/p denoising steps confounds sequence length with refinement iterations (non-standard choice), no fine-tuning evaluation

Modest scale (max 1.3B) and weak downstream absolute performance (20-38% accuracy), limiting confidence in ~4% relative improvements; unclear what drives the non-monotonic scaling of DiffuMamba (struggles at 0.5B, recovers at 1.3B) in Table 1
Inconsistent results between tables (e.g., DiffuTran's 153.47 PTB PPL vs. 43.82 validation PPL in Tables 1-2) with insufficient explanation
Limited statistical rigor: only 5 throughput runs with 3 warm-ups, no confidence intervals or significance testing; claims like '8.2×' are point estimates without uncertainty

Missing essential ablations and comparisons: no comparison with sparse or linear attention variants, no sensitivity to N value, no evaluation of bidirectional fusion alternatives, incomplete analysis of failure modes
